# What Notion API tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is, written out until the body is the length the pattern reads it
# at: forty-six characters behind ntn_, and forty-three behind the secret_ of
# the format Notion issued until September 2024. Neither count is an
# abbreviation — a body shortened for readability would leave a case holding no
# token at all — and each comes to the same fifty characters with its prefix in
# front.
#
# The cases under the over-match heading are not tokens and nobody issued them.
# What they hold is a name closing on the older prefix with a value spliced
# straight onto it, and a digest written behind a prefix, which are the two
# shapes fifty characters of this grammar can be reached by writing.

patterns: notion-api-token

# The two prefixes. One string serves every kind of token the Public API takes —
# the static token of an internal connection, the OAuth access token of a public
# one, a personal access token — so what is below differs in where a token
# stands rather than in what kind it is. The older prefix is read beside the
# newer because Notion did not revoke the tokens carrying it: the changelog
# announcing the change says they continue to work unchanged.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      NOTION_TOKEN=«notion-api-token»

case:     a token in the bearer header a request carries
in:       Authorization: Bearer ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      Authorization: Bearer «notion-api-token»

case:     a token in the response an oauth exchange returns
in:       {"access_token":"ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd","token_type":"bearer","workspace_id":"0123456789ab"}
out:      {"access_token":"«notion-api-token»","token_type":"bearer","workspace_id":"0123456789ab"}

case:     a token of the format issued until september 2024
in:       NOTION_TOKEN=secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      NOTION_TOKEN=«notion-api-token»

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd.
out:      the token is «notion-api-token».

# The alphabet a body is written in: base62, the letters of both cases and the
# digits, which is what every ruleset reading either prefix admits behind it.
# Neither character base64url adds is in it, so a hyphen ends a body where it
# stands, and so does a second underscore — which is the character a candidate
# is found by, and which no body carries.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       ntn_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCD
out:      «notion-api-token»

case:     a hyphen inside the body
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123-456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      ntn_0123456789abcdef0123-456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     a further underscore inside the body
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123_456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      ntn_0123456789abcdef0123_456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     an older-format body written in capitals
in:       secret_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789A
out:      «notion-api-token»

case:     a hyphen inside an older-format body
in:       secret_0123456789abcdef0123-456789abcdef0123456789
out:      secret_0123456789abcdef0123-456789abcdef0123456789

case:     a further underscore inside an older-format body
in:       secret_0123456789abcdef0123_456789abcdef0123456789
out:      secret_0123456789abcdef0123_456789abcdef0123456789

# How long a token is. Fifty characters, prefix included, read exactly rather
# than as a floor — which is where this pattern stands with the AWS, Google and
# SendGrid ones rather than with the OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe, PyPI and npm
# ones. Notion states no length at all; what the fifty rests on is that both
# published shapes come to it, the prefix having lost three characters when
# Notion changed it and the body having gained three.
#
# So a body of another length is not a token of another length. A run longer
# than the count is a token with something written after it, and only the token
# is redacted; a body shorter than its count — which is what a line cut to a
# column limit leaves — is no token at all, and every random character before
# the cut comes through in the clear. The cases below are both, and the second
# is here to be looked up rather than arrived at.

case:     an alphabet run longer than the body
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd0
out:      «notion-api-token»0

case:     a body one character short
in:       NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     a body of the older format one character short
in:       NOTION_TOKEN=secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789
out:      NOTION_TOKEN=secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789

case:     a token cut off at its prefix
in:       NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_
out:      NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_

# What a token may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of a
# match, as there is none in any built-in but the Slack and Stripe ones: a
# demand in front would drop a token written against a letter rather than trim
# it, and one behind would drop a token with a character of its own alphabet
# after it. What the count buys is the other side of that — a word written
# straight onto the end of a token is left where it stands, where the OpenAI,
# Anthropic, PyPI and npm patterns would read it as more of the body.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       NOTION_TOKEN_ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      NOTION_TOKEN_«notion-api-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      x«notion-api-token»

case:     a token inside quotes
in:       export NOTION_TOKEN="ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd"
out:      export NOTION_TOKEN="«notion-api-token»"

case:     a word written against a token
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdsuffix
out:      «notion-api-token»suffix

case:     a hyphenated word written against a token
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd-suffix
out:      «notion-api-token»-suffix

case:     a letter before an older-format token
in:       xsecret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      x«notion-api-token»

case:     a dashed word written against an older-format token
in:       secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a-suffix
out:      «notion-api-token»-suffix

# Two tokens written together. The characters in front of either prefix's
# underscore belong to the alphabet a body is written in, so a body closing with
# ntn hands the underscore written after the token to a candidate beginning
# three characters before that token ends, and a body closing with secret does
# the same six characters before. The underscore such a candidate is found by
# stands past the first token rather than inside it, so the scan reaches it; the
# two spans overlap and are redacted as one. Written without that overlap the
# two are separate values, and both go.

case:     two tokens separated by a space
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «notion-api-token» «notion-api-token»

case:     a token written straight onto the end of another
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      «notion-api-token»«notion-api-token»

case:     a token beginning inside the token before it
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789antn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      «notion-api-token»

case:     a token of the older format beginning inside the one before it
in:       secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «notion-api-token»

case:     the newer prefix in front of an older-format token
in:       ntn_secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      ntn_«notion-api-token»

case:     the older prefix in front of a newer-format token
in:       secret_ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      secret_«notion-api-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued, and the one place the text taken
# is text somebody wrote. secret_ closes an ordinary name — client_secret_,
# app_secret_ and webhook_secret_ are all that shape — so where forty-three
# unbroken letters and digits are spliced straight onto one, the name is
# redacted from its secret onward.
#
# What keeps such a name out of a span in an ordinary file is the character that
# follows it there: a file writes =, a colon and a space, or a quote between the
# name and the value, and none of those is a character a body is written with.
# The tightening on offer in front is the one the Slack and Stripe patterns
# take, to ask that no letter and no digit stand before the prefix, and it would
# not help — it admits the underscore, which is what every one of these names
# carries in front of the prefix. The pattern's own file weighs both.

case:     a name closing on the older prefix with a value spliced onto it
in:       client_secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      client_«notion-api-token»

case:     the same name with the value written where a file would write it
in:       client_secret=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      client_secret=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

# A digest written behind a prefix, which is the other shape reachable by
# writing. Hexadecimal digits are base62 and a digest carries nothing that ends
# a run, so a SHA-256 behind either prefix reaches the count and the first fifty
# characters are redacted — the rest of the digest stays in the text, which is
# what reading a count rather than a floor leaves behind. A SHA-1 is forty
# characters and an MD5 thirty-two, and neither reaches either count.

case:     a sha256 behind the prefix
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «notion-api-token»ef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha256 behind the older prefix
in:       secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «notion-api-token»bcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha1 behind the prefix, six characters short of a body
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an md5 behind the prefix
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, read in
# the case Notion writes it and in the character it closes with. The two after
# them are the count and the anchor: a body a space has broken, and a run of the
# right length behind an underscore that opens no prefix. Of the rest, a digest
# and a sentence carry no underscore at all and so hold no position to be found
# at however long they run, and the environment a Notion client is configured
# through is written in snake_case and does carry the anchor — what turns it
# away is the word after each underscore, which is far short of a body.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       NTN_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      NTN_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries its underscore
in:       ntn-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      ntn-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd

case:     an uppercase older prefix
in:       SECRET_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SECRET_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123 456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      ntn_0123456789abcdef0123 456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     a run of the right length behind an underscore that opens no prefix
in:       xyz_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      xyz_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd

case:     a run of the right length with no prefix at all
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef

case:     an environment file naming the token rather than carrying one
in:       NOTION_API_KEY=\nNOTION_VERSION=2022-06-28
out:      NOTION_API_KEY=\nNOTION_VERSION=2022-06-28

case:     a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.notion.com/v1/pages
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.notion.com/v1/pages

# Adjacency the properties in conformance drive on generated text but never
# assert an expected output for: a multi-byte rune, an invalid UTF-8 byte, a
# tab and a carriage return.

case:     a token between japanese
in:       日本語ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd日本語
out:      日本語«notion-api-token»日本語

case:     a token between tabs
in:       \tsecret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a\t
out:      \t«notion-api-token»\t

case:     a token followed by a carriage return and a newline
in:       token=ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd\r\n
out:      token=«notion-api-token»\r\n

# And a Notion credential this pattern has nothing to say about. A public
# connection is given a refresh token beside its access token, and that one
# opens with nrt_. Nothing published pins what follows it: the one example
# Notion prints is forty-nine characters where both token forms are fifty, and
# the one ruleset carrying a rule for it reads a range of forty to fifty-five
# and admits the underscore inside the body. A count guessed at there locates
# part of a token or none of it, so none is guessed at and the string below is
# left whole.

case:     a refresh token, which no count here is read for
in:       {"refresh_token":"nrt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd"}
out:      {"refresh_token":"nrt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd"}
